description:
<pre style='white-space:pre-wrap;width:81ex'>[dbt-schemas] Per-resource-type applicability table for warehouse config keys

* feat(schemas): per-resource-type applicability table for warehouse config keys

Adds `#[derive(WarehouseScope)]` (dbt-proc-macros) and applies it to
WarehouseSpecificNodeConfig via a `#[warehouse(...)]` attribute on the
struct and its fields. Generates `key_status(resource, key) -> KeyStatus`
and `all_keys()`, keyed on `dbt_telemetry::NodeType` so a typo'd variant
is a compile error rather than a silently-dead table row.

table (Valid/Stale/Invalid/Unknown), built as an alternative to splitting
WarehouseSpecificNodeConfig into one struct per resource type -- the split
struct membership is a one-bit valid/invalid encoding.

All 124 fields are annotated from today's Project<X>Config field lists;
nothing is marked stale here, so this PR changes no behavior. A
conformance test (table_matches_project_config_field_lists) reflects each
Project<X>Config's JSON Schema and asserts the table agrees with it
exactly, so this is provably inert and any future divergence between the
two config surfaces becomes a test failure instead of a silent drift.

See .agents/plans/.../2026-09-17-11963-warehouse-config-per-resource-type/
for the full design and phased rollout plan (not committed).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(schemas): deprecation warning + strip logic for stale/invalid warehouse keys

Adds ErrorCode::DeprecatedConfigKey (1057, free slot between
MissingTargetDirectory and ColumnTypeMismatch) and
warn_and_strip_deprecated_warehouse_keys, the shared logic each of the
four config-parsing surfaces (dbt_project.yml, in-file config(),
schema.yml for sql-backed resources, schema.yml for YAML-only resources)
will call before typing a raw config mapping:

- Stale keys are left untouched (still applied) and warn -- the canary's
  whole premise is that behavior does not change while a key is staged
  for removal.
- Invalid keys are removed from the mapping in place, before it reaches
  the existing unknown-key check, and warn.
- Valid/Unknown keys are untouched; Unknown still falls through to the
  existing UnusedConfigKey (1060) path unchanged.

DeprecatedConfigKey needs no warn-error-options registration: any
ErrorCode variant is already parseable by name there
(raw.parse::<ErrorCode>() in dbt-common's WarnErrorOptionValue parsing),
confirmed by a new dbt-error test.

Not called by anything yet (#[allow(dead_code)], to be dropped once the
next commits on this branch wire in the four call sites) -- this lands
first so the logic has its own tests, in particular
stale_key_is_kept_not_dropped, before anything depends on it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(loader): wire the deprecation canary into dbt_project.yml

Calls warn_and_strip_deprecated_warehouse_keys for each of the 7
warehouse-bearing dbt_project.yml sections (models, seeds, snapshots,
sources, tests, unit_tests, functions), on a clone of the raw mapping
before it is typed. raw_yml itself is left untouched, since it's
returned for provenance (unrendered_config / state:modified), which
needs the file's true authored content.

other three -- in-file config(), schema.yml for sql-backed resources,
schema.yml for YAML-only resources -- are follow-up commits on this same
PR). dbt_project.yml is first because it's the lowest-risk integration
point (a raw-YAML pre-pass, matching #11759's shape) and it's where
INC-6789 actually happened.

Two things verified empirically before and after this change (manual CLI
runs against a scratch project, not just unit tests):

- An Invalid warehouse key on this surface previously hit a hard
  SerializationError (1013) "Custom keys must go under +meta" the first
  time the project's nodes were resolved -- not the UnusedConfigKey
  (1060) warning path, which only covers null-valued keys. This is
  INC-6789's exact failure mode. It now warns (DeprecatedConfigKey, 1057)
  and the key is dropped before that error path is ever reached.
- A Stale warehouse key keeps applying: built a real seed project with
  `+immutable_where` (temporarily marked stale-for-Seed to exercise the
  path, then reverted -- deciding what's actually stale is follow-up
  work, not part of this commit), confirmed the 1057 warning fires *and*
  the authored value survives unchanged into the generated manifest.json.

Also fixed two bugs caught by these checks before they shipped:
- The per-scope closure was passing the `+`-prefixed key straight to
  `key_status`, which only knows bare field idents -- silently making
  every warehouse key "Unknown" and a no-op.
- A bare (non-`+`) nested scope name (a package or folder) must never be
  looked up in the table at all, even after stripping a hypothetical `+`
  -- a folder literally named `sort` would otherwise be misread as the
  `sort` config key and its entire subtree dropped. `warehouse_scope.rs`
  is a shared, surface-agnostic helper, so this `+`-vs-bare distinction
  is handled in the caller, not there.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(parser): wire the deprecation canary into schema.yml for sql-backed resources

Wires warn_and_strip_deprecated_warehouse_keys into the `config:` block
of model, snapshot, function, and data test schema.yml entries -- the
resource types that render a `.sql` file and share
`extract_model_config`/`render_unresolved_sql_files`. Sources, seeds,
and unit tests are YAML-only and go through their own bespoke
`into_typed_with_jinja` calls, not this shared path; they're follow-up
commits.

Also adds `WarehouseConfigResource` (const NODE_TYPE per resolved config
type) to dbt-schemas, implemented for all 7 resource types. Its test-
suite payoff: `table_matches_project_config_field_lists` now reads each
resource type off `T::NODE_TYPE` instead of a hardcoded `NodeType`
literal, so a typo'd impl (e.g. SeedConfig's const accidentally saying
Snapshot) fails there instead of only surfacing once something starts
calling it.

Those two are also used by `analyses` and `checks`, whose resolved
configs embed no warehouse fields at all. Adding a
`T: WarehouseConfigResource` bound there was the first attempt, but
resolving it generically at that layer is unsound: `key_status` would
return `Unknown` for basically every one of their keys, EXCEPT if one of
their own legitimate fields happens to share a name with a warehouse
field (e.g. `description`), in which case it would be misread as that
warehouse field and wrongly stripped, or spuriously flagged stale/
invalid. So this landed as a new standalone
`strip_deprecated_warehouse_keys_from_properties(node_properties,
resource)` that only the four warehouse-bearing resource types call
explicitly, rather than a bound satisfied implicitly by whichever
concrete type happens to be in scope.

Built a real YAML-block-style snapshot (`relation: source(...)`, no
`.sql` file) with a Model-only warehouse key (`jar_file_uri`, Invalid for
Snapshot) alongside a genuinely `all_nodes` key (`partition_by`, Valid)
and a real typo (`totally_bogus_config_key`):

- `jar_file_uri` -> DeprecatedConfigKey (1057) warning, absent from the
  generated manifest.json.
- `partition_by` -> present in the manifest, no warning.
- `totally_bogus_config_key` -> unchanged: still the original hard
  UnusedConfigKey (1060) error.

This specifically exercises the trickiest case: block-style snapshots
type `SnapshotProperties` (including `config:`) once early to extract
`relation`, then re-serialize the typed value back into `schema_value`,
which flows into `render_unresolved_sql_files` a **second** time. A
single strip call before that first typing pass was enough -- no
duplicate warnings, no key reappearing on the second pass.

Unlike the dbt_project.yml surface (previous commit), an Invalid key
here was previously **silently accepted** (it's just a field on the
shared struct), not a hard error -- so this commit is the first point
where behavior actually changes for those keys, from silent-apply to
warn-and-drop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(parser): wire the deprecation canary into schema.yml for source/seed/unit_test

Wires warn_and_strip_deprecated_warehouse_keys into the three
YAML-only resource types -- source, seed, unit test -- each of which
has its own bespoke into_typed_with_jinja::<XProperties, _> call rather
than sharing extract_model_config/render_unresolved_sql_files the way
model/snapshot/function/data_test do (previous commit). No `.sql` file
means no shared renderer to hook into; each of the three gets its
strip call inserted directly before its own typing call, on the
already-owned mpe right before it's consumed.

Sources are a source-and-table matrix (one MinimalPropertiesEntry per
(source, table) pair, all sharing the same source-level schema_value),
so a deprecated key on the source itself will warn once per table under
it -- matching how any other unknown-key diagnostic on this surface
already behaves for the same reason, not a new wart this commit
introduces. Table-level config (`Tables`/`TablesConfig`) needs no call
at all: confirmed it has no warehouse fields.

Verified empirically end to end for all three, including manifest
output:
- source: the exact scenario from the start of this investigation
  (immutable_where/engine/transient on a source) now warns and drops
  instead of nothing happening silently; a real unknown key is
  unaffected.
- seed: jar_file_uri (Model-only by the container default, so Invalid
  for Seed) warns and is absent from the manifest; quote_columns (a
  real field) and a genuine typo are both unaffected.
- unit_test: same jar_file_uri check, same result.

This completes the resolved (schema.yml) surface -- all 7 resource
types now route through the canary. Remaining in this PR: in-file
config() calls, and the JSON Schema pass for editor/LSP parity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(jinja): wire the deprecation canary into inline {{ config(...) }} calls

Wires warn_and_strip_deprecated_warehouse_keys into ParseConfig::apply_config
(dbt-jinja-utils), the shared handler for both `{{ config(...) }}` and
`config.set(name, value)` in a resource's own .sql file. This is the last

## Design: an explicit Option<NodeType> field, not a trait bound

build_resolve_model_context (and the ParseConfig it constructs) is shared
by every resource type that can render Jinja: model, snapshot, function,
data test, unit test (via resolve_given_seed's ref/source expression
context, not its own config -- see below), analyses, checks, exposures,
and operations. Six of those flow through dbt-parser's own
render_unresolved_sql_files/RenderCtxInner, but two go through totally
separate call sites (resolve_exposures.rs, resolve_operations.rs), and a
completely different crate (sdf-linter's rendered_linter.rs) calls
build_resolve_model_context directly too, generically over any node type,
for its own SQL-rendering-for-lint purpose.

Given that spread, a WarehouseConfigResource trait bound (used safely in
the schema.yml commit, where the type set was closed) is not an option
here -- the type/call-site set is open-ended and includes call sites this
change should not touch at all (the linter must not re-emit or duplicate
a parse-time warning). So resource_type is a plain `Option<NodeType>`
field threaded explicitly through RenderCtxInner -> build_resolve_model_
context -> ParseConfig, with each of the 9 call sites stating its own
value:
  - Some(NodeType::X) for model/snapshot/function/data_test (via
    RenderCtxInner, matching the schema.yml commit's resource types).
  - None for analyses/checks/exposures/operations (no warehouse fields).
  - None for the linter (parse-time concern, not its job) and for unit
    tests' resolve_given_seed (only ever renders a `given:` ref/source
    expression, never an inline config() call -- unit test config comes
    from schema.yml, already covered).

## Verified empirically end to end

A generic data test's inline config() call, tested directly (not just
unit tests): `jar_file_uri` (Model-only by the container default, so
Invalid for Test) warns and is absent from the manifest; `severity` (a
real field) is present; a genuine unknown key still hits the unchanged
original UnusedConfigKey (1060) hard error.

Also added 3 apply_config unit tests: an Invalid key is stripped from the
typed config, `resource_type: None` never strips anything, and a
dependency package's own config() call is exempt even when resource_type
is Some -- matching the "root project only" gate every other canary call
site uses.

cover (dbt_project.yml, schema.yml x7 resource types, inline config()).
Remaining in this PR: a JSON Schema pass for editor/LSP parity, and
eventually flipping specific (resource, key) pairs to Stale once this
table has been reviewed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(schemas): allow `description` on data tests, stop leaking issue refs into JSON schema

Two CI regressions from the warehouse-key deprecation canary

- `description`'s `#[warehouse(valid(...))]` list excluded `Test`, but
  generic data tests legitimately set `description` via their `config:`
  block (synthesized into an inline `{{ config(...) }}` call), which is
  a documented dbt-core-parity feature with no `dbt_project.yml`-side
  equivalent. Add `Test` to the valid list, and record the resulting
  departure from `Project<X>Config`'s field lists in a small, commented
  allow-list on the conformance test rather than letting it fail.
- The doc comment added to `WarehouseSpecificNodeConfig` was a rustdoc
  (`///`) block, which `#[derive(DbtSchema)]` promotes into the
  `"description"` field of every embedding resource's JSON Schema --
  leaking internal issue numbers and an `.agents/plans/` path into the
  customer-facing `dbt man --schema schema` output. Demote it to a
  plain (`//`) comment so it stays in the source but out of the schema.

* chore: trim verbose/issue-referencing comments across the warehouse-scope canary

Comments across this PR's diff had grown into paragraph-length design
each to a plain one- or two-line note describing what the code does,
with no issue-tracker references, and drop the "still to be wired in"
claim in warehouse_scope.rs that's now inaccurate (all four surfaces
are wired). No logic changes; comment/doc-comment text only.

* chore: further comment trims across the warehouse-scope canary

Continue reducing per-call-site comments to what the code doesn't
already say for itself: drop several one-liners entirely where the
call/field name already conveys it (resource_type: None, the strip
calls), shorten the WAREHOUSE_BEARING_SECTIONS and
strip_deprecated_warehouse_keys doc comments in dbt-loader, and
condense the unit-test given:-context comment to one line. Keep a
short note on the operations.rs None (NoOpConfig has no warehouse
fields) since the call site there has no name to lean on.

* chore: restore call-site comments, shorten derive/table doc comments

Add back one-line "why None" comments for analyses/checks/exposures
resource_type call sites (name alone doesn't convey it there). Shrink
the WarehouseScope derive's doc comment and a few warehouse_scope.rs
doc comments (WarehouseConfigResource, warn_and_strip_deprecated_
warehouse_keys, the all_keys-drift test note) down to their essential
points, dropping restated implementation detail.

* fix(schemas): make the warehouse-key canary warn-only on the resolved surface

Keys the applicability table marks Invalid still deserialize into
WarehouseSpecificNodeConfig on schema.yml and inline config(), so stripping
them there drops values that work today. Downgrade to Stale on that surface via
resolved_surface_key_status and keep stripping in dbt_project.yml, where
Project<X>Config has no field to deserialize into.

description:
fix: keep the microbatch event-time filter on relations derived from a ref

* fix: keep the microbatch event-time filter on relations derived from a ref

Closes #16392

Resolves dbt-labs/dbt-core#16383

### Problem

In a microbatch model, a relation derived from a ref, such as `{{ ref('x').include(...) }}`, drops the batch's event-time filter, so each batch reads the whole upstream table while the delete only covers the batch window. dbt Core keeps the filter.

`RelationObject::call_method` re-wraps the derived relation with `RelationObject::new`, which resets `run_filter` and `event_time`.

### Solution

`include`, `quote`, `replace_path`, `incorporate` and `without_identifier` now re-wrap through a helper that keeps the filter, matching dbt v1. `derivative`, `create_from` and `information_schema` point at a different object and are unchanged.

Tested with a `jinja_assert` test covering all five (it fails without the fix) and end to end on Snowflake, running microbatch models over a 2-day window of a 10-day source:

| Model reads | 2.0.6 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `ref('src')` | 2 rows | 2 rows |
| `ref('src').include(database=false)` | 19 rows | 2 rows |
| `ref('src').quote(...)` | 19 rows | 2 rows |
| `ref('src').replace_path(identifier=...)` | 19 rows | 2 rows |
| `ref('src').incorporate(path=...)` | 19 rows | 2 rows |

`without_identifier()` has no table to read, so it is covered by the unit test only.

description:
fix(benchmarks): stop reporting unscored leaderboard results as Fail (#1199)

## Summary

While looking at the `kaggle benchmarks leaderboard` flow, I found that
unscored results were being displayed as `Fail`.

The issue was with the `boolean_result` check. The SDK getter returns
`False` even when the field is not set, so checking `is not None` always
evaluates to `True`.

This caused results with no boolean or numeric score to be reported as
`Fail` instead of `N/A`.

## Fix

I changed the condition to use the SDK's field presence check
(`"boolean_result" in result.result`) so the CLI can distinguish an
actual `False` result from an unset field.

The change is kept minimal and only affects how leaderboard results are
displayed. Existing `Pass`, `Fail`, and numeric score outputs remain
unchanged.

## Tests

Added regression tests using real SDK objects created through
`ApiBenchmarkLeaderboard.from_json` instead of `MagicMock`.

The tests cover:

* Unscored results displaying as `N/A`.
* Actual boolean `True` and `False` results.
* Numeric scores, including `0.0`.
* Public/private score-only results.
* Mixed scored and unscored tasks in the same row.

Ran:

```bash
pytest tests/unit/test_benchmarks_leaderboard.py
pytest tests/unit
```

Results:

```text
20 passed
1381 passed, 10 subtests passed
```

Also ran the Black check for the changed Python files, which passed.

Updated `CHANGELOG.md` under `Next`.

This is a display-only change and does not affect the benchmark
scheduling or polling flow.

description:
fix(kernels): honor the version in // (#1201)

## Summary

`--help` for `kernels pull`, `output`, `status`, `files` and `logs`
describes the kernel argument as `//`, but
none of them honored the version. This sends it the way the API expects,
so each command acts on the version that was asked for.

## Problem

`pull` appended the version to the slug, which the API rejects with a
403. `output`, `status`, `files` and `logs` parsed it and then dropped
it, so they acted on the latest version. `logs --follow` put it in the
path of its streaming URL, which returns 404.

The worst case is `status`. On a notebook where versions 1 and 2
completed and version 3 failed, `kernels status /2` reported
`ERROR`, which is version 3's status under version 2's name.

## Solution

Every one of these requests accepts the version through `version_label`,
written as `v`. The bare number returns 404, which is the trap:

| request | sent | result |
|---|---|---|
| GetKernel | slug `.../1` | HTTP 403 |
| GetKernel | `version_label="1"` | HTTP 404 |
| GetKernel | `version_label="v1"` | version 1's source |

`_kernel_version_label` turns the number that `kernels push` prints
(`Kernel version 2 successfully pushed`) into `v2`. A value that is
already prefixed passes through unchanged, so `/v2` also works
and is never turned into `vv2`. Anything that is not a plain number is
left as the user wrote it.

The five commands now set `version_label` when a version is given.
Without one, the requests are exactly what they were, so the latest
version is still used.

`logs --follow` does not use a generated request. Its streaming endpoint
takes the same value as a `versionLabel` query parameter, and putting it
in the path returns 404. It now parses the kernel with
`parse_kernel_string` like the other commands, which leaves
`_split_kernel` without a caller, so it is removed. `--follow` was not
in #1200, but it is the same bug on the one path that streams.

## Behavior

Measured against the live API on one notebook with three versions: 1 and
2 completed and wrote `marker.txt`, 3 wrote `third.txt` and failed.

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `status /2` | `ERROR` | `COMPLETE` |
| `output /1` | `third.txt` | `marker.txt` from version 1 |
| `files /3` | `marker.txt` | `third.txt` |
| `logs /1` | version 3's log | version 1's log |
| `logs /1 --follow` | 404, exit 1 | version 1's log, exit 0 |
| `pull /1` | 403, exit 1 | version 1's source, exit 0 |

Without a version the requests are unchanged, so every command behaves
exactly as it did before. `/v2` behaves the same as
`/2`.

## Test changes worth pointing out

`test_kernels_pull_with_version` and `test_kernels_pull_with_metadata`
asserted `kernel_slug == "my-slug/3"`, which is the form that returns
403. They now assert `kernel_slug == "my-slug"` and `version_label ==
"v3"`. Nothing else about those tests changed.

## Testing

- [x] `hatch -e test run pytest tests/unit/test_kernel_versions.py -v`
(14 passed)
- [x] `hatch -e test run pytest tests/unit` (1384 passed, 3 skipped)
- [x] `hatch run lint:all`
- [x] Verified against the live API with the table above, including the
previous behavior on the same notebook
- [ ] Maintainer: please run `/gcbrun` when convenient

New tests cover the formatter, that `files`, `status`, `logs` and
`output` send the version, that `output` keeps sending it on every page
it walks, that an already prefixed version is not prefixed again, that
no version leaves each request as it was, and that `--follow` puts the
version in the query rather than the path. Eleven of the fourteen fail
against the previous code; the three that do not are the regression
guards on the no-version path.

Docs updated in `docs/kernels.md` and `skills/references/kernels.md`.
`kernels logs` has no section in `docs/kernels.md`, so it was left for a
separate change rather than written from scratch here.

## Related

Fixes #1200

This also resolves #442 and #525, which asked for the output of a
specific version.

description:
docs(skill): find the draw.io CLI outside PATH and off the C: drive

The Windows-native branch of "Locating the CLI" equated "installed" with
"on PATH or in C:\Program Files\draw.io". draw.io Desktop's installer does
neither: it never registers PATH, and the install directory is a free
choice, so an install on D: made the skill report the CLI as absent and
silently drop Mermaid conversion, ELK --layout and PNG/SVG/PDF export.

Give Windows the four-step chain it was missing — PATH (where.exe
draw.io), the default and per-user install paths, the registry uninstall
keys (InstallLocation / DisplayIcon, HKCU + HKLM + WOW6432Node), then
Program Files\draw.io on the remaining drives — plus a find-drawio.ps1
that runs all four and prints the first hit. WSL2 had the same blind spot
past its two C: paths: scan /mnt/*/Program Files and fall back to the same
registry values via reg.exe, translated back with wslpath -u. Only an
empty result across the whole chain now counts as "not installed", and a
CLI found off PATH is worth telling the user about.

Mirrored into the Codex and Copilot copies.

Closes #72

description:
fix(tool-server): load the shape index through the CDN cache

search_shapes fetched shape-search/search-index.json from jsDelivr with a
bare fetch(): no timeout (Node's undici defaults only give up after 300 s),
no disk cache (every process start re-downloaded ~400 KB brotli, ~1 s on a
fast link), and nothing to fall back to when the CDN is unreachable.

The index now goes through loadCachedSource like the ELK bundle and the
routing core: SHAPE_INDEX in cdn-cache.js with a 20 s budget (the ELK
bundle's, not the routing core's 5 s: the index is five times larger and a
100 KB/s link needs ~4 s for the transfer alone), an ETag-revalidated
per-user copy on disk (a warm start is a 304 in ~40 ms), and the last cached
copy when the CDN stalls, is unreachable or serves a truncated body. The new
src/shape-index.js wraps it so the JSON parse doubles as the cache validator
and the returned source is never parsed twice.

DRAWIO_SHAPE_INDEX_URL keeps working and, like DRAWIO_ELK_URL, now also
accepts a local file path. In-repo checkouts still read the local index and
never touch the network. test/shape-index.test.js covers the 200/304 cycle,
the stalled CDN with and without a cached copy, a truncated download, and
the local-path source against a local HTTP server.

Prompted by #71, which added a 5 s AbortSignal to the bare fetch.

description:
Added

  • Attendance approval helpers — adds shortcuts to calculate attendance approval duration, validate travel/out-of-office companion schedules, and query employees' effective complex overtime settings. Proposed overtime durations (total and per-day detail entries) must be finite positive numbers matched to the requested duration unit, and numeric detail-list work dates must be 13-digit millisecond timestamps; anything else is rejected before the server call. Flag help publishes each custom constraint's decision facts so the delivered schema keeps the validation contract visible to agents, and the detail-list help matches the two-stage workflow (second-stage input; the first stage omits it to obtain the server's per-day skeleton).

  • Auth status read-only snapshot — dws auth status --readonly observes the local credential snapshot without the authentication lock, network validation, refresh, migration, or credential writes, keeping the same output fields as normal status and reporting inconclusive local state through explicit reason codes instead of a confirmed logout.

  • Contact user lookup by dingtalkId — adds dws contact user get-by-dingtalk-id --id (alias search-dingtalk) to retrieve a user's userId from their dingtalkId.

  • 数字员工管理与能力资源 — 新增 dws dingtalk-tag manage、capability、run，覆盖创建、草稿保存、发布、查询、Skill ZIP 上传、员工域 MCP 创建与运行追踪；统一 agentUuid，支持双响应模式与 open_code / local_agent 类型。MCP 创建自动追加草稿依赖配套服务端，不自动发布；Skill/MCP 选择支持省略保留、空数组清空和非空数组替换。

  • 员工身份登录 — manage login 串联授权码申请、换票、在线身份核验和精确 Profile 保存/刷新，保持主管当前 Profile；补充外部 auth exchange，不在普通输出中返回授权码或 Token。

  • 本地 Agent 接入 — dingtalk-tag connect 支持本地 Agent Adapter 与 DSH，提供员工隔离的事件处理、生命周期、设备绑定及失败恢复；仅登录员工身份使用 manage login。同步 Help、Schema、mono/multi Skill 与必要接口文档。

  • 统一 dingtalk-tag manage 的 agentUuid / userId 用户契约：创建时部门可省略，草稿按字段更新并分开 Skill/MCP 输入，本地头像可安全上传且不暴露临时凭证。

  • 直属上级的输入与输出统一使用 supervisorUserId；HSF 历史字段名仅保留在 MCP 映射边界内部。

  • 头像统一使用 avatarUrl；--avatar-url 同时支持公网 HTTP(S) 与本地图片，本地文件复用 Skill 上传封装并自动回写。

  • 创建、更新的主程序类型映射到 MCP digitalTagEmployeeProfile.type；列表筛选仍使用顶层 type。CLI 保留 --main-program-type，详情查询改为 --snapshot draft|published 并发送 snapshot，兼容旧 --type 别名。

  • 创建时响应模式缺省或为空，默认发送 mention_only；更新未传则保留原值，显式响应模式不会被默认值覆盖。发布前的完整配置由服务端校验。

  • 登录/连接使用已发布详情的 profile.corpId/userId，不再要求旧 robotUid/staffId 字段；换票后仍在线核验身份，再保存精确 Profile。

  • MCP 创建/替换配置的帮助、Schema 与技能示例明确要求显式填写 configString.mcpServers.<名称>.type（streamable-http 或 sse），避免只有 URL 时服务端校验失败。

  • 创建数字员工必须显式指定 --main-program-type open_code|local_agent，DWS 本地拒绝缺失或空值，帮助/Schema/调用说明同步标为必填；更新不传仍保留原值。

  • Mail employee lookup by corporate email — adds mail user get --org-email
    and mail user batch-get --org-emails, with Schemas for
    mail.get_user_by_org_email and mail.batch_get_users_by_org_emails.
    Batch lookup accepts 1–100 addresses before deduplication and returns matched
    employees plus notFoundOrgEmails. Both declare required input mappings,
    read-only safety, and result fields, and use platform-injected operator and
    organization identity.
    Direct single lookup validates the employee result and declared field types
    before reporting success, while retaining null/omitted not-found results and
    exact integer IDs. This check does not reject a batch because one item is bad.

  • Mail batch partial results — preserves confirmed employee and not-found
    results when individual inputs or response records fail. Partial output
    separates succeeded, failed and unknown entries (exit code 7). An explicit
    server rejection of an invalid batch address falls back to at most 100
    deduplicated single-address lookups, including errors classified by the
    runtime transport; global authentication, permission and
    connection failures do not trigger that fallback. Unconfirmed results are
    never reported as not-found.
    Address-validation fallback recognizes the live service code 1001 as well
    as SYSTEM_ERROR; unrelated errors with either code remain failures.
    During fallback, global failures retain their original classification and
    exit status, with confirmed progress in structured error
    details.partialResult. Cancellation and raw PAT authorization errors are
    returned to the framework unchanged instead of becoming partial success.
    Agent guidance requires reading confirmed members from succeeded even on
    exit code 7, continuing authorized follow-up work with them and reporting
    unmatched, failed and unknown addresses.

  • Large integer output precision — preserves integer IDs beyond the exact
    float64 range when decoding MCP text responses and through --jq, --fields
    and formatted output.

  • International login is English-first — dws auth login --intl now renders
    its terminal copy, the DingTalk authorization page (lang=en-US) and the
    callback success page in English without requiring DWS_LANG=en. A locale
    inherited from LANG no longer forces Chinese output; set DWS_LANG=zh
    explicitly to keep the Chinese copy. Domestic (.com) login keeps following
    DWS_LANG/LANG as before.

  • Wait framework capability — adds the reviewed Contract.Wait
    declaration (contract.WaitSpec) with three execution modes: poll
    (cadence-poll the leaf's WaitPoll hook), event (consume the leaf's
    WaitEvents push stream, correlate events to the accepted resource via
    match_field/resource_query, apply the same terminal map), and auto
    (event first, fall back to polling when the stream ends or the
    subscription fails — one deadline spans both phases). Declared commands
    must use the ResultInvoke dispatcher; mode and hooks are paired at
    construction (poll↔WaitPoll, event↔WaitEvents, auto↔both; surplus hooks
    are rejected too). Declared commands register --wait /
    --wait-timeout (framework-owned flags that never enter MCP toolArgs);
    undeclared commands reject the flags as unknown. The wait phase closes
    the unified envelope exactly once: terminal success → success,
    terminal failure → failure with new wire-stable error.type: "wait"
    (exit code 8), timeout → pending with meta.operation.timed_out: true
    and the last observed state (exit 0). Deadline exhaustion during a poll,
    during event consumption, or between polls always closes as timed-out
    pending, never as a poll/stream failure; a correlated event with an
    unknown status fails closed exactly like a poll. The pairing also closes
    the overlay path: AttachContract / Tier2 metadata attaches cannot
    publish a wait declaration (no hooks, no flags, no wait phase behind
    it) — only the managed New construction can. At Schema assembly every
    poll_command is resolved against the bound registry and must name a
    delivered, agent-visible read command, so the declared manual resume
    path cannot drift from the command tree. The capability is
    projected into the Schema catalog (wait key) alongside dry_run. No
    business command declares it yet; approval/export/batch adoption lands
    separately.

Changed

  • Smart chat read shortcuts (+chat-messages, +at-me, +search-msg, +thread-replies) now decrypt third-party encrypted (SafeChat) message ciphertext before projection when the message crypto policy allows it. Message projections gain contentDecrypted, cryptoLayer, and dingKeyVersion (when > 0), and payloads gain an additive decrypt ledger (decryptCandidateCount, decryptAllowedCount, decryptedCount, decryptFailedCount, decryptFailures[]). Single-item failures land in the ledger with partial: true and never change the command exit code. Policy-off keeps the ciphertext and records one policy_disabled failure per candidate, so the additive ledger appears with decryptFailedCount >= 1 and the existing partial field can flip to true; only stub builds and --dry-run short-circuit the decrypt pipeline and keep output byte-identical to the previous behavior.

  • intField in the message crypto module now accepts json.Number, so keyVersion fields surfaced as JSON numbers by the MCP runtime are parsed instead of being silently dropped. The atomic chat read path may now emit dingKeyVersion on decrypted message projections (additive and within the existing result contract). Parsing ttlSeconds the same way means the crypto policy cache now honors the server-provided TTL: atomic reads fetch the policy once per conversation within the TTL window instead of once per message.

  • Introduce Schema delivery inside the existing Schema command of the single dws executable. Production does not produce or embed Schema identity at compile or release time. On supported ends (darwin/linux/windows amd64/arm64) each machine generates identity from live declarations at install or first dws schema, writes authenticated protobuf shards under the shared or user cache directory, and later hits verify digests then read those shards. Miss or corruption repairs from live assembly; when the shared cache exists but cannot be locked for repair (typically root-owned read-only), the repair falls back to the per-user cache and later processes reuse it. Empty local identity generates then uses the cache; it is not a permanent live-only mode. When plugins or other runtime extensions change the command surface, cache assembly and repair are delegated to an isolated child process using the pristine pre-registration environment, keeping persistent cache active without inheriting plugin runtime side effects. Plugin commands never enter the Schema surface, cached or live. The POSIX installer only advertises a cross-user shared cache when the warmed artifacts are root-owned, matching the runtime's shared-path ownership rule; a cache warmed by an ordinary user under a writable custom root is reported as installing-user-only instead.

  • Keep one complete Cobra tree for every public invocation. Compact typed metadata and shared builders reduce complete-tree allocations; process argv does not select a product factory or a utility-only tree.

  • Reduce temporary allocations during Schema validation and command initialization.

  • Normative notes live in docs/rfc-schema-runtime-cache.md only; no sibling plan/design/performance pages are kept.

Removed

  • Retire legacy contract review CLI leaves — hide dws contract review benefit|create|analysis|result from help and mark their Agent Schema availability unavailable. The commands remain as hidden historical argv stubs and fail closed with command_retired without calling legacy review MCP tools. The review group stays visible because hiding it is not in the consumed ledger. Ledger schema_availability_hardening entries are consumed.

Fixed

  • OA TableField examples (#1347) — correct mono and multi skill examples to encode detail rows as a two-dimensional array of name/value objects, and clarify that both creation modes preserve the serialized value without converting row objects.

  • Persistent Schema cache with plugins (#1400) — delegates Schema cache assembly and repair to an isolated child process when plugins are present, keeping persistent cache active without inheriting plugin runtime side effects.

  • AI Table form sharing now exposes server-returned shareFormUuid, status, and cover through shared structured result contracts for atomic commands and shortcuts; updates also publish cpSynced. Agent guidance requires confirming CP synchronization before reporting the sharing workflow as complete. Readback and CP projection remain the server's responsibility; DWS does not issue a second view update or construct cover URLs.

  • Atomic and shortcut updates now share strict terminal validation. Missing or invalid required fields, including cpSynced=false, produce partial_failure (exit 7), preserve the remote response and mark remote execution as started without retrying the write. Result Schema documents both verified success and partial-stage evidence. Usage guidance distinguishes supplied IDs from placeholders and preserves the shortcut JSON flag.

  • Terminal validation binds baseId, tableId, and viewId to the original request before accepting CP synchronization. A complete response for a different form is still partial_failure, even with cpSynced=true; both command entries retain the raw response and never replay or compensate the write.

  • Terminal validation also compares the explicitly requested enabled, formName, and formDesc against the echoed readback, so a response reporting different values is partial_failure rather than success. Requested properties the helper never echoes cannot be proven, so verified success reports verified=false and lists them in unverified instead of implying they took effect.

  • All four form-share Result Schemas accept their real dry-run request previews, including the optional shortcut dry_run marker. Preview success never implies remote execution or CP synchronization; assembled-leaf regression tests validate real envelopes against both full and compact JSON Schemas.

  • Skill discovery preserves the requested atomic/shortcut entry for result reviews instead of substituting usage Help. Interpretation selects the actual result branch and does not invent required fields or copy Schema evidence into malformed samples.

  • Recovery reviews preserve the target named in the original user request before Skill loading. Agent-authored Skill arguments cannot turn a background write into an additional contract-review target; this scope boundary is visible in discovery metadata as well as the loaded body. Synthetic JSON receipt reviews also load the product Skill: prohibiting online business operations does not skip local contract discovery or permit generic guesses about product-specific fields.

  • AI Table write recovery: +table-copy and +record-batch-create now generate one UUID v4 clientToken per create batch, submit it once, and reconcile uncertain receipts through MCP get_record_write_result. A fully recovered ID set is independently checked against record values before continuing. Unknown or partial results preserve the token/IDs and stop without replaying creation. The new read-only +record-write-result command exposes the recovery path in Help and Schema.

  • AI field readiness: +field-create recognizes MCP CREATE_FIELD_READBACK_PENDING, keeps the created IDs, and uses the existing bounded exact-ID readback/resume path. +field-run-ai requires readable aiConfig before mutation and reports submitted only for complete per-field task receipts; submission is not computation completion.

  • Review follow-up: duplicate-token errors and explicit get_record_write_result recovery hints no longer count as input rejections, even with retryable=false. They use the original token for read-only reconciliation and value verification; ordinary input rejections still stop immediately.

  • Recovery evidence: unknown creates without returned IDs do not advertise known effects. The read-only reconciliation command includes its Intent, and its Result Schema distinguishes verified applied results from dry-run previews and rejects unknown or incomplete success objects.

  • Pagination recovery: record queries classify business errors before accepting an empty terminal page. Invalidated cursors discard accumulated records and continuation tokens, return non-retryable restart guidance, and stop composite workflows before further writes.

  • Agent recovery guidance: the Shortcut Schema and mono/multi pagination references distinguish invalid snapshots from ordinary resumable failures; stale snapshots must discard prior rows and cursors, never deduplicate and concatenate pages across snapshots or replay a composite write.

  • Pagination review boundary: mono/multi references separate a concise, complete recovery assessment from operational query recipes. Unknown or incomplete writes remain read-only until reconciled; comparing query results is not permission to infer missing records or propose incremental create/backfill.

  • Focused recovery discovery: field-create Help/Schema explains CREATE_FIELD_READBACK_PENDING and bounded same-ID verification. Result-only reviews stay on the requested recovery command instead of expanding to its upstream write command or inferring unpublished Result fields from repeated discovery.

  • Skill loading and routing: keep the AITable skill description focused on capability selection, with execution examples in the loaded body. Contract reviews preserve the requested command identity and query only that command, without treating background writes as additional discovery targets. Regression tests enforce this metadata/body boundary and all four exact form-share review routes.

  • Recovery review clarity: lead with the requested read-only next step and safety decision, distinguishing local contract discovery from unverified remote state. When no command is requested, answer all safety questions up front—write replay, retained/discarded results, and read-only recovery prerequisites—before detailed explanation. Unknown or incomplete results retain the original Base/Table/token reconciliation route instead of switching to full-table queries. Reconciliation Schema explicitly treats records missing from the returned ID set as unverified, never as a count-based backfill plan.

  • Deployment dependency: the paired MCP branch must be deployed and the new read-only tool registered in the gateway. No lippi-doc-notable changes are included. Local mock/contract tests do not establish live service readiness; real-environment evaluation remains a separate deployment check.

  • 登录过程中使用临时 Token 补全身份时，立即应用本次登录的 MCP 端点覆盖，包括国内及国际预发；不再等待登录成功后的 mcp_url 持久化。显式产品端点、第三方地址和插件所属路由保持原值，查询不读取旧 Profile。

  • Windows 原生覆盖率作业的总时限从 20 分钟调整为 30 分钟，为完整测试批次、工具链准备和产物上传保留余量，避免接近 20 分钟的运行被取消。测试范围、单批测试超时、100% 变更代码覆盖率门禁及汇总依赖检查保持原有要求。

  • DEK missing relogin — Allow reauthorization when the local login encryption key is missing. Keep old ciphertext until a fresh credential is available, then replace only the login write targets and create a new encryption key as needed. Refresh and transient Keychain failures retain their existing protection.

  • 数字员工 Skill 创建和更新使用同一个已打开的文件完成 ZIP 校验与流式上传，避免校验后重新打开路径时把替换文件或符号链接目标上传。上传仅读取校验时的文件大小，句柄在操作结束（包括 dry-run 和失败）后关闭。

  • 补充普通文件替换和符号链接替换的 create/update 回归测试，保留打开前对命名管道等特殊文件的拒绝；增加 dingtalk_tag.skill_package_validated、dingtalk_tag.file_upload 本地诊断事件，仅记录大小、阶段、接口路径、成功状态与耗时，不记录本地路径、文件内容、身份或凭据。

  • 修正数字员工接入的事件传输就绪判断：使用上游真实状态并报告断线重连，区分 IPC、Agent 初始化和事件连接；DSH 状态交叉验证同一员工的 Event Bus，旧版或未知连接不再报告传输就绪。

  • 数字员工本地 Agent 不再固定指定事件来源为 digital_employee，改为沿用 Event 默认规则：优先读取 DWS_STREAM_SOURCE_ID，未设置时开源版使用 open；升级后需重启员工 worker 生效。

  • 个人 Stream 正确响应系统 ping/disconnect，不将系统控制帧投递为业务消息；订阅查询兼容 items/list 及字符串/整数时间戳。

  • 修正 Windows 下正常停止可能被误报为消费者异常退出，以及损坏的任务/绑定目录被误当作不存在的问题；补充跨平台身份、绑定回执、上传失败、重试隔离和日志脱敏回归测试。

  • 单聊引用回复 — 会话信息明确返回 singleChat: true 时，即使省略群聊话题开关，也能正常引用回复；保留会话身份、响应有效性及话题标记校验。

  • OA approval event fields — preserve staff_id, activity_id, corp_id, and business_id from the business payload in event consume --flatten for all seven OA approval events, and expose cc_time for approval instance CC events. Optional fields remain omitted when absent; an explicitly provided zero cc_time is preserved.

  • Legacy token pre-login recovery — Allow OAuth, device, auth-code, PAT, and --token reauthorization to start when the legacy auth-token ciphertext has a confirmed DEK mismatch. The old ciphertext remains untouched until fresh credentials are available, then only the login's target slots are replaced; transient and unclassified Keychain failures still fail closed.

  • Windows cgo 崩溃：重新编译 Windows amd64/arm64 预编译 libsafechat.a（消除 legacy _vsnprintf/__imp__* dllimport 引用），并移除已无必要的 msvcrt_compat_windows.c 旧 CRT 桥接层，修复官方发布包在 Windows 上初始化 safechat（cgo）即崩溃的问题。

  • Root help renders the live complete Cobra tree, so explicitly registered supplement-backed commands stay visible alongside products and utilities. There is no separate declaration-derived help snapshot.

  • Command validation errors — report framework-owned parameter failures consistently as validation errors with exit code 3, while preserving API errors, explicit exit codes, cancellation, and deadlines.

  • Parent and proxy flags — route parent traversal and wiki proxy parse failures through the same validation boundary and preserve target command hints.

  • Required flag wording — framework-prepared commands now report missing required flag(s): --name instead of Cobra’s required flag(s) "name" not set. The original Cobra error remains available as the cause.

  • Generated commands — normalize native validation failures in lazily created help/completion commands, and remove duplicate required/group checks while retaining business hook order.

description:
fix(docx): a style's set places its children in CT_Style / CT_RPr order

`set /styles/` inserted a missing direct child at the END of the
w:style element and let the SDK particle order the children of a style's
w:rPr. Both landed children where neither CT_Style nor CT_RPr puts them,
and the SDK validator then rejected the document (issue #434):

  set /styles/Normal --prop basedOn=Title
  ->    (basedOn after pPr)
     validate: unexpected child element 'w:basedOn'

  set /styles/Heading1 --prop highlight=yellow
  -> ...          (highlight first)
     validate: invalid child element 'w:highlight'

name / aliases / basedOn / next / link all precede pPr and rPr in
CT_Style, so the tail append was only ever wrong on the INSERT path -
a style that already owned the child was edited in place, which is why
`set /styles/Heading1 --prop basedOn=...` validated cleanly.

The style-rPr half has a second cause. ISO/IEC 29500-4 CT_Style declares
 - the same complex type a run's
w:rPr uses - but SDK 3.4.1's compiled particle for StyleRunProperties is a
truncated CT_RPr: 35 children against RunProperties' 51, missing rStyle,
highlight, rtl, cs, oMath and the w14 extension block (its typed class has
no Highlight/RunStyle/... property either). Since the comparator sorts what
it cannot recognise to the FRONT, SchemaOrder.Place hoisted 
ahead of . SchemaOrder now borrows the RunProperties particle
for that one container; for every element both particles declare the
relative order is identical, so only the five undeclared ones and the w14
block move - measured, not assumed (see the PR description).

Both halves are the same defect class in the same command path: a style
child is appended rather than placed. The containers get the same
treatment, so a table style (tblPr/trPr/tcPr present, no rPr) no longer
ends up with rPr after them.
product_or_resource: fix(docx): a style's set places its children in CT_Style / CT_RPr order

Two defects on the MCP surface, both verified through a live stdio session:

description:
Resolve store list --organization-id without listing every organization

`store list` fetched the account's whole organization list before it even
looked at `--organization-id`, using it only to validate the flag and to
read the organization's name — which `ListAccessibleShops` already returns.

Move the single-organization lookup the app client already had into
`@shopify/organizations` and use it from `store list`, so an explicit
`--organization-id` costs one cached lookup instead of a full listing.

`organizationsWithAccessToDestination` requests no `first` and no
`pageInfo`, so the listing is whatever single page Business Platform
returns. A lookup by ID can't be truncated that way. It is also unfiltered,
since the schema offers no `APPS_CLI` filter for it, so it can resolve an
organization the account belongs to but can't reach from the CLI — the
org-scoped shops request stays the authority there, and such an
organization now reports no stores rather than not found.

A miss still falls through to the filtered list, which supplies the
accessible organizations for the error and re-resolves access granted
since the cached miss.

Key the lookup's cache by a hash of the Business Platform token. The
GraphQL cache key covers only the query, the variables and the CLI
version, so the cache `orgFromId` has been using answers one account's
lookup with another's organization.

description:
fix: repair Windows code signing (#727)

* fix: repair windows code signing on current runner images

The sign-windows-release job failed at the "Setup Certificate" step with
"/d/Certificate_pkcs12.p12: No such file or directory". GitHub's Windows
runner images no longer expose a D: drive, so decoding the DigiCert client
cert to /d/ aborts the job before signing is ever attempted.

Write the cert to $RUNNER_TEMP instead, which is what twilio-csharp's
code-signing job already does, and align the rest of the signing path with
that workflow:

- add the digicert/code-signing-software-trust-action SSM setup step
  (same pinned SHA as twilio-csharp)
- drop the hardcoded --keypair-alias from "smctl windows certsync". It was
  added mid-debugging in Feb 2026, corrected once, and no run has been green
  with it present; the last successful release (Jan 2026) and twilio-csharp
  both use the plain form.
- replace ::set-output with $GITHUB_OUTPUT

windows-executable-draft-release.yml carried the same /d/ bug plus a
signtool.exe path pinned to SDK 10.0.17763.0, which is no longer present on
the runners. Port the release workflow's dynamic signtool discovery over,
add the certificate listing step for parity, move to windows-latest-large,
and bump the v2 checkout/download-artifact actions in the signing job.

The signing commands themselves stay different by necessity: signtool takes
a SHA-1 thumbprint (/sha1), nuget sign takes SHA-256
(-CertificateFingerprint). Same certificate, different fingerprint per tool.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* fix: strip carriage returns before decoding the signing cert

The Setup Certificate step now reaches the decode (the $RUNNER_TEMP path
fix landed) but fails with "base64: invalid input". The secret is stored as
wrapped base64 and git-bash coreutils rejects \r as invalid, so pipe it
through tr first. twilio-csharp runs the same command successfully, so the
difference is in the stored value, not the command.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* fix: use the x64 signtool so the Keylocker KSP can load

signtool found the certificate ("Done Adding Additional Store") but
SignerSign() failed with 0x8009002D (NTE_FAIL). The step was selecting the
x86 signtool, while DigiCert's Keylocker KSP ships x64-only
(Keylockertools-windows-x64.msi) - a 32-bit process cannot load it, so the
failure lands at the private key operation rather than at cert lookup.

Prefer x64 (newest SDK first), fall back to x86, and add /v /debug so any
further provider error is legible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* chore: add smctl healthcheck before signing

signtool now selects the correct certificate and reports a private key
association, but SignerSign() still fails with 0x8009002D, which points at
the DigiCert side rather than Windows plumbing. smctl healthcheck reports
client tool, credential and keypair status, and keypair ls shows which keys
this identity may actually sign with. Non-fatal so it cannot block a run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* chore: fingerprint the decoded signing cert

smctl healthcheck reports the client certificate path or password is
incorrect, while read-only operations succeed - signing is the only step
needing client-cert mTLS. The password reaching smctl is correct, so print
the size and sha256 of the decoded .p12 to confirm whether the stored
secret matches the local copy. Also widen the whitespace strip, since the
value was wrapped when it last failed to decode.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* chore: verify the decoded p12 opens with the password secret

Comparing hashes across machines proved unreliable - the logged sha256 came
back with a stray byte and only 61 hex characters. Test the pair in place
instead: have openssl try to open the decoded container with
SM_CLIENT_CERT_PASSWORD and print only the verdict. This settles whether
the two secrets match each other, which is what smctl healthcheck is
complaining about.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* chore: add smctl sign as a diagnostic step

The p12 and password are verified consistent on the runner (openssl opens
the container, and it does contain a private key), yet smctl healthcheck
still reports the client certificate as incorrect and signtool fails with
0x8009002D. signtool gives no detail, so run DigiCert's own signer against
the same keypair first; it reports actionable errors. Non-fatal, so the
existing signtool step still runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* fix: save credentials into the DigiCert store for the KSP

REST hash-signing against both keypairs succeeds with the same API key,
client cert and password (HTTP 200, real signatures), so the credentials
and the SIGN_SM_HASH authorization are correct. The failure is therefore in
the Windows KSP that signtool and smctl sign both load, not in DigiCert.

smctl reads credentials from the environment, but the KSP is a separate
component and may only read DigiCert's credential store. Save them there
before signing. Prints the command help too, since the exact flag spelling
is unverified. Non-fatal, and healthcheck now runs after it so its report
reflects the saved state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* fix: correct the smctl credentials save invocation

The previous attempt passed --cert-file, which smctl rejected with
"unknown flag", so nothing was ever saved. Per smctl credentials save
--help the command takes two positional arguments, API_KEY and
CLIENT_CERT_PASSWORD, and stores them in the OS credential store; the
certificate path continues to come from SM_CLIENT_CERT_FILE.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* chore: remove signing diagnostics now that signing works

Signing succeeded in run 35881288396: healthcheck reports 2FA and signtool
reports "Number of files successfully Signed: 1".

Root cause was the client-auth .p12 being exported with OpenSSL 3's default
AES-256/PBES2 encryption. smctl is Go, and Go's PKCS#12 support only handles
legacy PBES1, so it could not parse the container, reported the client
certificate as incorrect, left the session at 1FA, and the KSP then failed
SignerSign() with 0x8009002D. Re-exporting the .p12 with legacy encryption
fixed it; that requirement is now documented at the Setup Certificate step.

Removals:
- the smctl sign diagnostic, which signed the artifact a second time
- the openssl probe in Setup Certificate; it could not distinguish the two
  container formats, since OpenSSL 3 reads legacy ones without -legacy
- /v /debug from signtool

Kept: the Keylocker healthcheck, which diagnosed this, and the credential
store save.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* revert: restore windows-executable-draft-release.yml to main

This change set is scoped to the release workflow only. The draft workflow
still carries the same /d/ cert path and the signtool.exe path pinned to SDK
10.0.17763.0, which will need the same treatment separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* docs: correct the signtool architecture comment

The previous comment claimed a 32-bit signtool cannot load the Keylocker
KSP. That was a hypothesis while chasing 0x8009002D and it did not hold:
switching to x64 changed nothing, the real cause was the PKCS#12 encryption
format, and the x86-first selector added in 8d61cdc signed successfully as
recently as the 2026-01-07 release.

Keep the x64 preference, since that is the combination verified working in
run 35881288396, but state the reasoning accurately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* docs: trim the signtool architecture comment

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* chore: drop the healthcheck step and make credential save fatal

The healthcheck was added to diagnose the signing failure and is no longer
needed now that the cause is known and documented.

Remove continue-on-error from the credential save: it was a probe when
added, but if that step ever fails silently the symptom is signtool failing
with 0x8009002D much later, which is the confusing failure mode this change
set exists to avoid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5

description:
fix: restore the aws-sdk devDependency (#726)

Oclif Release failed in run 35704797653 at the S3 upload:

  oclif-dev: uploading targets
  Error: Cannot find module 'aws-sdk/clients/s3'
  aws-sdk is needed to run this command.
  Install aws-sdk as a devDependency in your CLI.

@oclif/dev-cli needs aws-sdk to upload to S3 but declares it only in its own
devDependencies, which npm never installs for a dependency. It has to be a
devDependency of this package, and it was until #705 removed it:

  85b3e14 feat: add API standards support ...
  -    "aws-sdk": "^2.1361.0",

The timing matches: the last successful Oclif Release was 2026-02-18 and #705
landed after it, so this has been broken since, just unexercised until now.
Restores the exact version that was removed.

Not related to pinning Node 22 in #725: setup-node ran, the pack succeeded,
and the job reached the upload before failing.

aws-sdk v2 is end-of-support and @oclif/dev-cli is deprecated in favour of the
oclif v4 CLI already used elsewhere in this repo, which bundles AWS SDK v3 and
needs no aws-sdk devDependency. Migrating oclif-release.yml to it is the real
fix, but it changes what reaches S3 and Homebrew and needs its own validation;
this unblocks the release in the meantime.

Lockfile regenerated with --package-lock-only and passed through
restore-lockfile-registry.js, so the resolved URLs stay on registry.npmjs.org.
npm ci reports package.json and the lockfile in sync.

description:
fix: make the release prepare stage actually work (ESM import + tagFormat) (#720)

* fix: load semantic-release's default export and scope the dry run

The prepare stage failed with:

  TypeError: semanticRelease is not a function
      at getNextRelease (.github/scripts/next-release.js:15:24)

semantic-release is ESM-only from v22, so requiring it from CommonJS yields
the module namespace rather than the function; the callable is on .default.
Resolving .default || module handles both shapes, and an explicit check now
fails with a clear message instead of a TypeError if that ever changes again.

The require also moves inside the function, so loading this module no longer
depends on semantic-release being installed.

While here, the dry run is scoped to commit-analyzer and release-notes-
generator, taken with their options from .releaserc.json so the version
matches what the real release computes. Loading the publishing plugins made
this step depend on npm and GitHub auth it has no business needing: it
publishes nothing, and the npm trusted publisher is bound to the workflow that
actually publishes, not to this one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 

* fix: declare tagFormat so the dry run finds the existing tags

Mirrors twilio/twilio-cli-core. Tags in this repo are bare (6.2.4), not
v-prefixed. The publish command has always passed -t ${version} to match, so
the CLI was never affected. The programmatic dry run added in #719 gets no CLI
flags, so it fell back to the default v${version}, matched none of the tags,
and would have reported no previous release.

That would not have failed loudly. prepare-release.js would have written the
wrong version, and verify-release-version.js calls the same getNextRelease, so
the guard would have computed the same wrong version, matched, and passed --
while the publish step, which does pass -t, released the right one. npm would
have got a version the repo did not claim: exactly the mismatch this flow
exists to prevent, with the guard complicit because it shared the bug.

Declaring tagFormat in .releaserc.json gives both callers one value rather
than leaving the CLI flag as the only source. The -t flag is now redundant but
is left in place, since the publish path could not be exercised locally.

No past release was affected: next-release.js landed in #719 and has never
run here.

Verified against main in a worktree: computes 7.0.0 from lastRelease 6.2.4
(major, from the BREAKING CHANGE in #713 requiring Node 22), writes
package.json, both package-lock version fields and CHANGES.md, and the guard
then passes on that tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5

description:
[1.38.2] — 2026-09-25

Fixed

  • A 200 response from signal-cli's daemon can still carry per-recipient send failures (e.g. UNREGISTERED_FAILURE, IDENTITY_FAILURE) nested in a results array — previously returned as if the send succeeded. _rpc now raises SignalError when it finds one.
  • receive_direct never checked the signal-cli subprocess's exit code, so a failed receive silently returned an empty/partial message list instead of raising.
  • _ensure_contact_cache/_ensure_group_cache caught bare Exception, meant to tolerate "daemon not up yet" but actually swallowing any bug in the cache-refresh path. Narrowed to SignalError so real bugs propagate instead of silently leaving the cache permanently unpopulated.
  • Several RPC call sites (list_contacts, list_groups, list_sticker_packs, get_user_status, list_accounts, create_group, join_group) silently substituted an empty list/dict when signal-cli returned an unexpected shape, which read to the caller as "you have no contacts/groups" instead of an error. Now raise SignalError naming the RPC method.
  • get_webhook_url returned None for a corrupt/unreadable webhook.json, indistinguishable from "no webhook configured". Now raises RuntimeError.

Bugs identified via a diff against faces-sh/signal-mcp's fork; fixed directly against our existing SignalError/RuntimeError types rather than adopting the fork's envelope architecture.

Added

  • Read-only mode. Set SIGNAL_MCP_READONLY=1 to run the server with every state-mutating tool (send, edit, delete, react, group/account management, scheduling, desktop import, etc.) hidden from list_tools and rejected by call_tool if called directly. 24 read-only tools (contacts, groups, conversations, search, export, status) remain available.

Hardened

  • Stale plaintext temp files are swept at the start of every Desktop import — the only thing that can clean up after a SIGKILL, which no signal handler can catch.
  • SIGTERM/SIGINT now delete the in-flight plaintext temp file before the process exits (main-thread only, per Python's signal module constraints; the sweep above is the backstop for the background-thread case).
  • A single-flight lock prevents two concurrent Desktop imports from racing on the same local store.

Testing

  • webhook.py coverage: 39% → 100%.
  • 8 previously-untested MCP tool handlers (set_webhook, get_webhook, find_contact, schedule_message, list_scheduled_messages, cancel_scheduled_message, run_scheduled_messages, submit_rate_limit_challenge) now covered.
  • Fixed a long-standing order-dependent flaky test (test_ensure_group_cache) caused by unreset module-level cache state between tests.

fix: daemon CLI command now writes/clears the PID file

The `signal-mcp daemon` command (what the LaunchAgent runs) never
called save_daemon_pid/clear_daemon_pid -- only the auto-spawn path in
client.py's ensure_daemon() did. stop_daemon and the stale-PID cleanup
in ensure_daemon had no way to find a daemon started this way, and the

description:
fix: stop silently swallowing/misreporting signal-cli RPC errors

Cherry-picked 5 bug fixes found by diffing faces-sh/signal-mcp's fork
against ours, using our existing SignalError/RuntimeError types rather
than adopting the fork's envelope architecture:

- _rpc now raises SignalError when a 200 response carries per-recipient
  failures (e.g. UNREGISTERED_FAILURE) nested in a 'results' array.
- receive_direct now checks the signal-cli subprocess's exit code
  instead of silently parsing empty/partial stdout on failure.
- _ensure_contact_cache/_ensure_group_cache narrowed from `except
  Exception` to `except SignalError`, so real bugs in the cache-refresh
  path propagate instead of leaving the cache permanently unpopulated.
- list_contacts, list_groups, list_sticker_packs, get_user_status,
  list_accounts, create_group, join_group now raise SignalError on an
  unexpected RPC result shape instead of silently returning an empty
  list/dict.
- get_webhook_url now raises RuntimeError for a corrupt/unreadable
  webhook.json instead of returning None indistinguishable from "no
  webhook configured".

Also fixed test_list_conversations_resolves_group_names, which relied
on ambient global cache state populated by other tests hitting the
live signal-cli daemon on this machine — the narrowed exception
handling correctly stopped swallowing respx's AllMockedAssertionError
there, surfacing that the test wasn't hermetic.

description:
Minor Changes

  • f2a4f53: Add the slack Codex marketplace, giving developers a production install path for the Slack plugin in Codex:

    codex plugin marketplace add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin
codex plugin add slack@slack

    Until now the only marketplace this repo published was named slack-dev, so installing the plugin meant adding a marketplace labelled "dev" and running codex plugin add slack@slack-dev.

    If you installed under the old name, remove it before re-adding: Codex treats the two marketplaces as unrelated and will leave both installed and enabled.

    codex plugin remove slack@slack-dev
codex plugin marketplace remove slack-dev

  • 8044341: Support developer sandboxes, free, and paid teams as install targets, instead of treating a developer sandbox as the only option. create-slack-app Step 3 now presents a sandbox (recommended), a Free Team (second choice), or an existing production workspace (last resort, usually gated by admin app approval), and test-slack-app accepts a Free Team as a safe place to test. Also runs sandbox list and sandbox create non-interactively with --team, --name, and --password.

Patch Changes

  • 1579a07: Improve the docs.slack.dev page with clearer formatting. Document the slack-docs skill, which finds and reads official Slack dev docs as clean markdown to answer questions about the Slack platform.

  • b1c9af0: Ensure "run my Slack app locally" prompts route to the slack-cli skill rather than create-slack-app. The create-slack-app description previously advertised "creating + running a project from a Bolt template locally", overlapping with slack-cli's territory; dropping "+ running" disambiguates the two.

  • f1deaff: Document installing the skills with npx skills, which reaches coding agents beyond the three with a plugin surface:

    # Install the skills for a coding agent, named by its own identifier
npx skills add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin -y -a <agent>

# For example, Gemini CLI or OpenCode
npx skills add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin -y -a gemini-cli
npx skills add slackapi/slack-skills-plugin -y -a opencode

    This path already worked and needed no changes here, it was just undocumented. It carries the skills only: no commands, and no MCP server.
